nodes.label: staging.workflow_run_state (provider-agnostic table)
nodes.rationale: Schema is provider-agnostic (repo/run_id/conclusion/name/ts) so GitHub Actions and Jenkins both write into it and DORA queries need not know which tool built a commit — no migration needed to add Jenkins.

nodes.label: Layered Schemas (staging/core/mart)
nodes.rationale: Single Postgres with staging/core/mart schemas; mart is fully rebuildable from staging, preserving a clean migration path to ClickHouse/warehouse without touching ingestion or the API contract.

nodes.label: Queue-Isolated Connector Services
nodes.rationale: One connector service per tool publishing to RabbitMQ absorbs vendor outages via backoff+queue buffering (FR-1.8) and makes a new connector a new service+binding with zero core change (NFR Extensibility).

nodes.label: Event Envelope Contract
nodes.rationale: Thin envelope with raw vendor payload passthrough keeps connectors free of business logic (ADR-0002) so everything is reprocessable from staging and schema evolution never requires a connector redeploy.

nodes.label: Idempotency Key (source, sourceId, eventType)
nodes.rationale: Matches staging.raw_event unique constraint so redeliveries and backfill replays are no-ops and never double-count a metric.

nodes.label: RabbitMQ Topology (aiimpacteval.events)
nodes.rationale: Topic exchange with {source}.{eventType} routing + selective consumer bindings lets connectors and consumers be added independently; DLX quarantines poison messages rather than dropping them.

nodes.label: normalizeJenkinsResult
nodes.rationale: Maps Jenkins SUCCESS/FAILURE/UNSTABLE/ABORTED onto the lowercase success/failure/cancelled vocabulary metrics-engine's DORA queries hardcode, so every Jenkins build matches and metrics-engine needs zero changes.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md — AI Agent Rules & Documentation Policy
nodes.norm_label: claude.md — ai agent rules & documentation policy

nodes.label: Core Technology Stack
nodes.rationale: React+TS+Tailwind / Java 21+Spring Boot 3 / PostgreSQL 16 chosen to match internal expertise for fastest onboarding; Node full-stack and Python/FastAPI rejected as discarding Java/Spring expertise the BRD wants to leverage.

nodes.label: Vision — trustworthy real-time delivery + AI ROI view
nodes.norm_label: vision — trustworthy real-time delivery + ai roi view

nodes.label: No Manual Tagging Dependency
nodes.rationale: All metrics derived automatically from tool data (BO-2) so engineers never change how they work; garbage-in-garbage-out is designed out.

nodes.label: No Surveillance Features (ethical exclusion)
nodes.rationale: Permanent BRD §5.3 product invariant: no keystroke/idle-time/screen monitoring; individual views opt-in and growth-framed — surveillance perception is the top adoption risk.

nodes.label: AI adoption & ROI in financial terms (BO-3)
nodes.norm_label: ai adoption & roi in financial terms (bo-3)

nodes.label: Dev-Token Bridge
nodes.rationale: A config-gated, audited POST /api/v1/auth/dev-token issues role-scoped tokens so RBAC can ship and be tested ahead of OIDC; disabled in real environments and to be superseded by an OIDC ADR.
